simple.meaning: שִׁקְמָה (shiqmâh) appears 7 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a son in the family line and in connection with kingship and in connection with prophetic witness.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in 1 Kings, 1 Chronicles, 2 Chronicles, Psalms, Isaiah, and 1 more, beginning at 1 Kings 10:27. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family line, kingship, prophetic witness, land.

simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows שִׁקְמָה through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.

definitions.full: H8256. shiqmah [ שִׁקְמָה ] noun feminine sycomore tree (Late Hebrew id. , Aramaic שִׁיקְמָא ,, Löw No.332 ; hence Greek συκάηινος mulberry Lewy Fremdw.23 ); — plural absolute שִׁקְמִים Amos 7:14 +; suffix שִׁקְמוֺתָם Psa 78:47 ; — sycomore, ficus sycomorus Linn (Tristr NHB397ff. Post Flora of Syria 730 ; Hast. DB under the word) a common tree Isa 9:9 , growing in the Shephela 1Kin 10:27 = 2Chr 1:15 = 9:27 , 1Chr 27:28 ; as property Psa 78:47 (|| גֶּפֶן ); שִׁקְמִים בּוֺלֵס Amos 7:14 a tender of sycomores (see [ בַָלס ]).
